content.title: About
content.content: Cottage cheese, farmer's – a fresh curd made from whole milk of pasture‑raised cows without growth hormones. It has a mild creamy flavor with a slight tang and a smooth, crumbly texture. It can be eaten on its own, added to dishes, or used in baking.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cottage cheese is one of the oldest dairy products, known since ancient Egypt.
Farm‑raised cottage cheese is usually free of preservatives and stabilizers, making it a “cleaner” product.
It comes in various fat contents, from non‑fat to 9 % and higher.
In some regions cottage cheese serves as a base for cheeses like “ragout” and “spreadable” varieties.
It is often served with herbs, honey, berries, or used as a filling for pancakes and dumplings.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Cottage cheese provides high‑quality milk protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Calcium supports bone and tooth health and plays a role in muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Its low sugar content makes it suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains vitamin B12, riboflavin, and niacin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Probiotic potential
items.content: Natural farmer’s cottage cheese may contain live lactic‑acid bacteria that support gut microbiota.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: People with lactose intolerance may experience bloating, gas, or diarrhea after consuming cottage cheese.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Allergic reactions to casein or whey can occur in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some farmer’s versions are lightly salted; those monitoring sodium should check the label.

items.title: Shelf life
items.content: Cottage cheese spoils quickly; keep it refrigerated and consume within a few days.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy cottage cheese as a snack, blend it into smoothies, add to salads, casseroles, dumplings, pancakes, or use as a spread for crackers. It pairs well with berries, honey, nuts, or fresh herbs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cottage cheese in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C. It can be frozen, but the texture will change – after thawing it is best used in cooked dishes.

nutritional-powder-mix-whey-based-nfs.title: Nutritional powder mix, whey based, NFS (5495)

content.title: About
content.content: The NFS (5495) whey‑based nutritional powder mix is a fast‑dissolving supplement designed to support muscle recovery and provide essential nutrients after training. It contains high‑quality whey protein, vitamins, minerals and amino acids.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Whey protein is rapidly absorbed, delivering amino acids to muscles quickly.
The blend is fortified with B‑vitamins that play a role in energy metabolism.
Electrolytes (sodium, potassium, magnesium) help restore fluid balance.
The product is lactose‑free, suitable for those with lactose intolerance.
Each package provides 30 servings, with one serving weighing 30 g.

items.title: Supports muscle growth
items.content: High whey protein content promotes muscle protein synthesis after exercise.

items.title: Accelerates recovery
items.content: Branched‑chain amino acids (BCAA) help reduce post‑workout muscle soreness.

items.title: Restores electrolyte balance
items.content: Sodium and potassium aid hydration and nerve‑muscle function.

items.title: Boosts energy metabolism
items.content: B‑vitamins assist in converting food into usable energy.

items.title: Supports immune function
items.content: Vitamin C and zinc contribute to normal immune system activity.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Contains whey protein, which may trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Excessive protein intake
items.content: High consumption can strain kidneys, especially in people with pre‑existing kidney conditions.

items.title: Artificial sweeteners
items.content: Some versions may include sucralose or aspartame, which are not suitable for everyone.

items.title: Medication interactions
items.content: Large amounts of vitamin K can affect the efficacy of anticoagulant drugs.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Mix one serving (30 g) with 250‑300 ml of water or milk and consume immediately after training. It can also be added to smoothies, oatmeal or yogurt.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place, tightly sealed. Keep moisture and direct sunlight away. See the package for the expiration date.

pizza-with-meat-other-than-pepperoni-fro.title: Pizza with meat other than pepperoni, thin crust

content.title: About
content.content: A thin‑crust pizza topped with tomato sauce, mozzarella cheese and a variety of meats other than pepperoni (e.g., ham, chicken, beef). This version is commonly offered by fast‑food restaurants and pizzerias.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Thin crust is made with a small amount of yeast, giving it a crisp texture.
Meat combos without pepperoni allow experimentation with flavors such as smoked ham or barbecue sauce.
In some countries a meat‑only pizza without pepperoni is considered a “healthier” option due to lower processed sausage content.
The classic Italian “Marinara” is a pizza without cheese but with meat, inspiring modern pepperoni‑free versions.
Thin crust cooks faster in high‑heat ovens (400‑450 °C).

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: The meat provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Beef and chicken supply iron, important for oxygen transport in the blood.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Mozzarella is a good source of calcium, supporting bone health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat and yeast‑based dough contain B6, B12 and niacin, which aid metabolism.

items.title: Easily digestible carbs
items.content: Thin crust has less starch than thick crust, making it easier on digestion.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Salt in the sauce, cheese and processed meat can raise blood pressure if consumed frequently.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Meat and cheese contain saturated fats that, in excess, may contribute to cardiovascular disease.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: People with lactose intolerance or milk‑protein allergy should choose a dairy‑free cheese alternative.

items.title: Food‑borne infection risk
items.content: Undercooked meat may harbor pathogenic bacteria; the pizza should be cooked until fully done.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Thin crust contains gluten and is not suitable for individuals with celiac disease.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the pizza hot, sliced into wedges. Add fresh vegetables, basil or hot sauce to taste. It pairs well with a light salad or a cold beverage.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Reheat in an oven or grill to restore crust crispness.

content.title: About
content.content: Potato salad with light mayonnaise is a classic dish made from boiled potatoes, light mayonnaise, herbs, and sometimes additions such as eggs, cucumbers, or ham. Light mayonnaise contains less fat and calories than traditional versions, while still providing a creamy texture and pleasant taste.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Potato salad became popular in Europe in the 19th century and quickly turned into a staple for picnics and celebrations.
Light mayonnaise is often made with yogurt or plant‑based oils, reducing saturated fat content.
Traditional recipes include green onion, dill, and parsley, which boost aroma and add vitamin C.
Potatoes are usually diced into uniform cubes to ensure even coating with the dressing.
The salad can be prepared ahead of time, but it’s best to add the mayonnaise just before serving to keep the potatoes from becoming mushy.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Potatoes provide starch that offers sustained energy and a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Light mayonnaise contains less saturated fat, which is beneficial for cardiovascular health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Potatoes contain vitamin B6, important for protein metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Potassium
items.content: Potatoes are a good source of potassium, supporting normal blood pressure.

items.title: Fiber from herbs
items.content: Fresh herbs add dietary fiber, aiding digestion.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Light mayonnaise often contains added salt; people monitoring sodium intake should watch portion size.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Traditional light mayonnaise may contain eggs; those with egg allergies should use a vegan alternative.

items.title: Bacterial growth
items.content: When left at room temperature for more than 2 hours, the salad can become a breeding ground for bacteria.

items.title: Glycemic index
items.content: Potatoes have a high glycemic index, so individuals with diabetes should consider portion size.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the salad chilled as a side dish or a main light meal. It pairs well with fish, grilled chicken, or vegetable appetizers. Garnish with extra herbs or thin slices of radish before serving.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Stir before serving to redistribute the dressing. Discard if it develops an off‑odor or discoloration.
